messages:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: DEPLOY ALERT: canary for release v20250422-7 -> inference-service exceeded error-rate threshold (5m ERR% > 2.5). Rollout paused and auto-rollback attempted. Rollout id: r-20250422-7-canary

Maya Chen: paging @oncall - seeing 502/503 in canary, customers hitting failures on text-generation. Can we confirm fallback?

oncall-bot: @Raj Patel is oncall for infra. Paging now. Incident severity: P2 (customer-facing but partial impact). Escalation to eng-sre if not acknowledged in 5m.

Raj Patel: acknowledged. Looking. Can someone paste the canary metric window and affected routes?

Maya Chen: routes: /v1/generate (gen-large), /v1/chat. Traffic split 10% canary. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/abc123/inference-canary?var-release=v20250422-7 (error spike starts ~23:40 UTC).

Neal Ortiz: grabbing logs now. Early glance: model runner OOM on 16G instances, but the process crashed with allocator error, then k8s restarted. Could be a new kernel change in runtime image.

Sasha Li: Is this the rollout that enabled the new attention-kernel flag? That was gated by feature-flag `ff-accel-attn-v2`.

Maya Chen: yes, we enabled `ff-accel-attn-v2` in canary. If this is the kernel causing crashes we should kill the flag and rollback.

Raj Patel: auto-rollback kicked but controller shows "rollback stuck: pod crashloop on terminating". I want to avoid partial state where canary keeps flapping. Plan: 1) force rollback manually if auto fails 2) flip kill-switch for feature flag 3) verify customer paths back to stable. Who can run manual rollback?

Neal Ortiz: I can take step 1. Commands I'm going to run: 
```
# check rollout
kubectl -n services rollout status deploy/inference-service-canary --timeout=60s
# manual rollback to previous stable revision
kubectl -n services rollout undo deploy/inference-service --to-revision=124
# or via helm
helm -n services rollback inference-service 3
```

Maya Chen: after rollback, we should also purge prefix KV cache for canary traces and invalidate any cached prompt templates. Otherwise some requests might hit mixed model variants. Run: `redis-cli -h redis-canary del key:prefix-*` (Ops only).

LaunchDarkly-bot: Feature flag `ff-accel-attn-v2` toggled OFF for environment: production-canary by Sasha Li. (https://app.launchdarkly.com/projects/redwood/environments/production-canary/flags/ff-accel-attn-v2)

Sasha Li: yes I turned the flag off ~30s ago. Confirmed via LD console and API. Will monitor if pods recover after rollback.

Raj Patel: Neal, run the rollback. I'll coordinate with Maya on traffic and customer comms. 

Neal Ortiz: running commands now. Output: 
```
$ kubectl -n services rollout undo deploy/inference-service --to-revision=124
deployment.apps/inference-service rolled back
Waiting for deployment "inference-service" rollout to finish: 0 of 6 updated replicas are available...
```
Rollout progressing but see 2 pods stuck in Terminating state on node gpu-12 with SIGKILL during preStop. Killing those pods and letting controller recreate.

Raj Patel: I'm force-deleting stuck pods: `kubectl -n services delete pod inference-service-canary-7b9 --grace-period=0 --force`. Monitor for PV/volume detach issues.

Maya Chen: Customer impact update: internal monitoring indicates failed requests dropped from ~8% to ~0.4% across the board since rollback started. A subset of customers on eu-west saw latency spikes — ops tracing shows retries. Customer success notified for top 5 paying tenants.

Neal Ortiz: new pods coming up on nodes gpu-08/gpu-09, logs show model started and healthcheck passed. `kubectl get pods -n services` shows READY 6/6 for inference-service now.

Raj Patel: verifying traffic routing: envoy metrics show canary traffic back to stable model (version 20250421-3). Confirming config: `curl -s http://mesh-config/local/backends | jq .routes["/v1/generate"].backend` -> returns inference-service:stable.

Sasha Li: double-check A/B variant: run a few synthetic requests against stable and verify token outputs look reasonable. I ran a smoke test: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"sum 2+2"}'` -> 200 OK, expected content.

Maya Chen: noted. I'm preparing a short incident summary for customers and CS: root cause appears to be interaction between `ff-accel-attn-v2` kernel change and memory usage on our GPU instance profile. We're tagging this P2 and will escalate to research for deeper investigation.

Eng Oncall: handoff: Eng Oncall will monitor for 60 minutes, then escalate to eng-runtime if errors reappear. Raj, Neal, Sasha, please keep watch and add any follow-ups to the incident board.

Raj Patel: setting an incident Slack thread pinned note and creating a follow-up ticket: INF-2124 "Investigate attention kernel OOM when ff-accel-attn-v2 enabled". Assigning to eng-runtime and research.

Neal Ortiz: saving logs and container dumps: `/var/log/pods/inference-service-canary/*` archived to s3://redwood-ops/incident-1718574321/ for postmortem.

Maya Chen: CS message drafted: "We experienced elevated errors on text-generation during a canary rollout. We paused the rollout and rolled back to the previous stable model; service is healthy. We're investigating root cause and will share remediation timeline." Will post after Raj signs off.

Raj Patel: sign-off on customer note. Post to status page and ping top customers.

Sasha Li: quick reminder for rollout hygiene: add a canary resource limit bump test to the CI job and a preflight OOM smoke run against 1/100 synthetic traffic. I'll open a PR to add that.

Maya Chen: thanks all. Incident closed from active mitigation perspective. Handoff to Eng Oncall for monitoring; Neal/Raj/Sasha will be on async follow-up. Will create postmortem template and assign reviewers. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Auto-note: rollback completed and verified by 3 approvers. Incident annotated: rollback_method=manual, feature_flag_killed=true, customer_impact=partial.

Eng Oncall: monitoring for 60m. If error rate > 1% again, re-open this thread and escalate to eng-runtime.

(End of thread)
